question.problem:
An eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}]$ 
corresponding to an eigenvalue $\lambda =3k-2$ is $[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5k\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5k\end{aligned}] & =(3k-2)[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5k\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -30+35k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6(3k-2) \\ (5k)(3k-2)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -30+35k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-18k+12 \\ 15{k}^{2}-10k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6=-18k+12 \\ -30+35k=15{k}^{2}-10k\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $k$ in the first equation, we get

$$
-6=-18k+12\,⟹\,k=1.
$$

Now, substituting $k=1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-30+35k & =15{k}^{2}-10k \\ -30+35\cdot 1 & =15\cdot {1}^{2}-10\cdot 1 \\ 5 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a true statement.

Therefore, the solution of the system is $k=1.$
